intro: The library contains twenty reference scenarios that cross at least three domains. They are reference patterns: each assessed Capability Instance shall instantiate the applicable scenarios against its own architecture, parameters and evidence, and shall not cite a library scenario as evidence. Durations, thresholds and capacities are capability-profile parameters; where an example value is given it is labelled illustrative.

scenarios.title: Utility voltage sag during a synchronous training load swing
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A transmission-system fault produces a voltage sag at the point of connection that exceeds the UPS input tolerance, followed within seconds by a sustained utility interruption from protection operation upstream.
scenarios.preconditions: A large synchronous training job is running with periodic power swings between compute and communication or checkpoint phases (swing magnitude and period are capability-profile parameters). UPS modules operate in a high-efficiency mode with a transfer time to inverter. Generator load-acceptance capability was verified with resistive load banks in steps, not with dynamic load. The utility interconnection agreement may contain requirements on load fluctuation.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → EMERGENCY (on battery, generators starting) → DEGRADED (on generators) → RECOVERY (retransfer to utility) → NORMAL; FAILED for affected blocks if load acceptance fails.

path.text: Sag TRIGGERS UPS transfer from mains or high-efficiency mode to inverter; batteries carry the full IT load including the swing (EXTERNAL_EVENT).
Utility interruption TRIGGERS generator start; UPS battery energy DELAYS consequence for the battery runtime at current state of health (WITHIN the runtime parameter).

When generators close onto the bus and UPS rectifiers walk in, the training load swing CONTRIBUTES_TO repeated large load steps on the generators; synchronous phase alignment across the job AMPLIFIES the step (DEMAND_SURGE).

Generator governor and AVR response produces frequency and voltage excursions; UPS rectifiers reject the generator source when frequency leaves their input window and return to battery, which CONTRIBUTES_TO further battery depletion (CONTROL_ACTION, AND with step 3).
Repeated rejection AND reduced battery state of health lead to battery exhaustion on one or more UPS blocks before stable generator supply is accepted (SEQUENCE).
Loss of output on those blocks PROPAGATES_TO the racks they serve; dual-corded racks whose second feed is on a surviving block ride through; single-path rack-scale systems drop.
Node loss in any participant TRIGGERS failure of the whole synchronous job (CASCADE); training progress since the last durable checkpoint is lost.
If CDU pumps or chilled-water pumps are on the affected blocks or are not UPS-backed, loss of flow PROPAGATES_TO surviving racks as a thermal transient (SHARED_RESOURCE).
Restart of all affected jobs at once creates a restore demand on checkpoint storage (links to X04).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-POW-01, RF-POW-02, RF-POW-03, RF-POW-06, RF-CAP-01, RF-THM-02, RF-CMP-01, RF-STO-03
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Training job completion and tolerated loss of progress (performance, recoverability); cluster availability (availability); compute capacity during the generator period (capacity)
safeguards: Cause side: workload power smoothing (power capping, ramp-rate limiting or on-site energy buffering) that bounds swing magnitude and ramp rate to the plant's characterised acceptance (interrupts step 3).

Escalation: generator sizing and governor/AVR tuning verified against the measured AI load profile; UPS rectifier walk-in and input-window settings coordinated with generator capability (interrupts step 4).
Escalation: UPS battery runtime at end-of-life capacity sized for repeated retransfer attempts (DELAYS step 5).
Consequence side: mechanical-cooling and CDU pumps on UPS-backed supply (interrupts step 8); scheduler-level checkpoint interval matched to tolerated loss (limits step 7).
scenarios.familyText: CAP-04 Demand and growth modelling; CAP-05 Operating envelope; POW-02 Generation and fuel; POW-03 UPS and energy storage; POW-05 Power quality and transient response; THM-06 Thermal control, maintenance and recovery; STO-05 Checkpoint and recovery services
evidence: E3 high-resolution power-quality recordings of the actual training load profile at UPS output and site level (magnitude, ramp, frequency content).

E4 integrated test of generator acceptance with a dynamic load profile representative of the AI load (programmable load bank or controlled workload), including UPS rectifier behaviour, witnessed (V6).
E7 generator transient-response study against ISO 8528-5 performance class and the measured profile; UPS coordination study.
E2 configuration extract of power-capping or ramp-limit settings on the fleet, reconciled to the approved value.
E3 battery state-of-health measurements and runtime test results.
scenarios.unknowns: Generator behaviour under dynamic AI load not tested (U5; US4 on CG-05). Swing profile of the next model generation unknown (U1; US3 unless it changes the envelope, then US4). Utility fault-level and sag statistics not provided (U2; US3).

scenarios.title: CDU pump-controller firmware fault causes loss of TCS flow
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A CDU controller firmware release mishandles a failed differential-pressure sensor reading and commands both duty and standby pumps to a minimum or stopped state, or enters a watchdog reset loop.
scenarios.preconditions: The same firmware version was deployed to all CDUs of that model across the hall within a short window. Standby pump start depends on the same controller. No hardwired fail-safe keeps a pump running on controller fault. IT-side power capping on coolant-flow loss is not configured. OEM remote support is required to diagnose controller faults.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL (or TRANSITION during rollout) → EMERGENCY → FAILED for affected racks → RECOVERY.

path.text: Defective release, deployed through the CDU management tool, is a LATENT condition in all CDUs (COMMON_CAUSE).
Sensor fault TRIGGERS incorrect controller action; both pumps stop (M09 then M01 on RF-THM-02); because the standby depends on the same controller, redundancy is DEFEATED.

Loss of TCS flow PROPAGATES_TO cold plates; low thermal inertia means accelerators reach thermal limits within the TCS ride-through time (a capability-profile parameter, illustratively tens of seconds).
Accelerators throttle and then hardware thermal protection shuts them down (M23 on RF-CMP-01).
The synchronous job fails (CASCADE); progress since the last checkpoint is lost.
Further CDUs with the same sensor condition fail the same way; failures CORRELATE_WITH the firmware release.
Diagnosis waits for OEM remote support (DELAYS recovery); manual pump override may be the only immediate recovery.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-THM-02, RF-THM-08, RF-THM-01, RF-CMP-01, RF-SUP-01, RF-SUP-03
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Training throughput and completion; compute capacity of affected rows; potential equipment damage if thermal protection is slow or disabled
safeguards: Cause side: staged firmware rollout with canary CDUs and defined soak period; pre-deployment test of sensor-fault handling (interrupts step 1).
Escalation: independent standby pump control or hardwired fail-run on controller fault; pumps default to running at safe speed on loss of control (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: coolant flow and pressure alarms independent of the CDU controller, feeding the BMS and the IT power-management system to cap power before thermal limits (DELAYS step 3).
Consequence side: scheduler placement spreading jobs across CDU fault domains where feasible; checkpoint interval (limits step 5).
Recovery: documented manual override procedure, practised; firmware rollback package held locally.
scenarios.familyText: THM-03 Liquid cooling systems; THM-06 Thermal control, maintenance and recovery; SUP-04 Software, firmware and update supply; SUP-06 Remote support and third-party access; OPS-05 Change and configuration management; CMP-05 Compute health and observability
evidence: E4 test record of sensor-fault injection on a non-production CDU with the deployed firmware, showing fail-run behaviour (V5).
E2 firmware inventory per CDU showing version distribution and rollout waves.
E4 measured TCS ride-through after pump trip at representative load (time from flow loss to accelerator throttling), V6 under controlled conditions.
E3 alarm and event history showing flow-loss alarms reach operators and power-capping triggers.
E1 change record with canary results and approval.
scenarios.unknowns: CDU controller failure behaviour on sensor fault not documented by OEM (U2 or U9; US4 on CG-06/CG-07). Whether standby pump control is independent (U10; US4). TCS ride-through at current density (U1; US4).

scenarios.title: PFC storm in a RoCE fabric from a misconfigured switch
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A switch configuration change maps lossless traffic class priorities inconsistently (for example a DSCP-to-priority mismatch or a buffer threshold error), or a faulty NIC continuously transmits priority flow control (PFC) pause frames.
scenarios.preconditions: The scale-out fabric uses RoCE with PFC for lossless transport. PFC watchdog (storm detection) is disabled or set with a long timer. Congestion control (ECN-based) is tuned for steady state, not for incast during collectives. Configuration templates are pushed by a fabric controller to many switches.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL or TRANSITION (during change) → DEGRADED → FAILED for affected jobs → RECOVERY.

path.text: Misconfiguration or faulty NIC TRIGGERS persistent pause generation on one port (CONFIG_DRIFT or HUMAN_ACTION).

Pause PROPAGATES_VIA inter-switch links hop by hop; head-of-line blocking spreads to unrelated flows sharing the priority; cyclic buffer dependencies can create PFC deadlock (SHARED_RESOURCE, AMPLIFIES).
Collective operations (all-reduce, all-gather) stall cluster-wide because every rank waits for the slowest (CASCADE).
Collective timeouts TRIGGER job failures across many jobs, not only the job on the faulty port.
If storage traffic shares the fabric or priority, checkpoint writes stall (MASKS the last-good checkpoint state).
Telemetry shows link-level health as normal (links up), which MASKS the cause and DELAYS diagnosis.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-NET-01, RF-NET-02, RF-NET-03, RF-CMP-03, RF-STO-02
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Collective communication performance; training throughput; job completion across the cluster; checkpoint durability
safeguards: Cause side: pre-deployment configuration validation of QoS and PFC consistency across the fabric; staged change with blast-radius limits (interrupts step 1).
Escalation: PFC watchdog enabled with timers shorter than collective timeouts, disabling PFC or dropping on the offending queue (CONTAINS step 2).
Escalation: congestion control (ECN marking thresholds, rate control) validated under incast; deadlock-free routing design.
Consequence side: storage traffic on separate fabric or priority (interrupts step 5).
Detection: pause-frame counters and queue telemetry with alerts (interrupts step 6).
scenarios.familyText: NET-01 Scale-up and scale-out fabrics; NET-02 Performance and congestion control; NET-03 Storage and service networks; NET-06 Network control and observability; OPS-05 Change and configuration management
evidence: E2 configuration extract showing PFC watchdog enabled and QoS mapping consistent on all switches, reconciled to the template.
E4 controlled pause-injection test in a test fabric or isolated partition with the production software version, showing watchdog containment time (V5/V6).
E3 fabric telemetry history of pause counters and ECN marks during large collectives.
E1 change records showing staged rollout and validation gates.
scenarios.unknowns: Watchdog behaviour on the deployed switch software (U1; US4 on CG-09). Whether storage and compute share a lossless priority (U4 if documents disagree; US3). Deadlock freedom of the routing scheme (U9; US4).

scenarios.title: Checkpoint storage saturation extends recovery beyond tolerance
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A facility event (for example X01) terminates many training jobs at once; operators and schedulers restart all of them simultaneously.
scenarios.preconditions: Checkpoint tier sized for steady-state write bandwidth, not for concurrent full-cluster restore. Checkpoint retention policy leaves little free capacity. Metadata service is a single scaling domain. Restart admission is not rate-limited.
scenarios.operatingStates: FAILED → RECOVERY (extended) → DEGRADED → NORMAL.

path.text: Simultaneous restart TRIGGERS a read storm against the checkpoint tier (DEMAND_SURGE).
Read demand exceeds tier throughput; metadata operations from many ranks opening shards create a metadata hotspot (M15 on RF-STO-03) which AMPLIFIES latency.

Before the event, retention had filled the tier so recent checkpoint writes failed silently or were truncated; the last verified checkpoint is older than expected (LATENT, CONTRIBUTES_TO progress loss).
Storage fabric congestion from the storm PROPAGATES_TO other tenants and to provisioning traffic (SHARED_RESOURCE).
Restore time across the cluster exceeds the recovery tolerance; accelerators sit idle (DELAYS recovery).
Timeouts during restore cause repeated restart attempts that AMPLIFY the storm (positive feedback).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-STO-02, RF-STO-03, RF-STO-01, RF-RES-04, RF-NET-03, RF-CMP-03
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Recovery time objective for training; tolerated loss of progress; compute capacity utilisation during recovery
safeguards: Cause side: restart admission control in the scheduler (staggered, priority-ordered restore) (interrupts step 1).

Escalation: checkpoint tier and metadata service sized and tested for concurrent restore of the declared job population; tiered checkpointing using node-local storage with asynchronous drain (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: capacity headroom alarms and retention enforcement; checkpoint completion verification before the previous checkpoint is released (interrupts step 3).
Consequence side: QoS isolation of storage traffic (CONTAINS step 4); exponential back-off on restart retries (interrupts step 6).
scenarios.familyText: STO-02 Performance and capacity; STO-05 Checkpoint and recovery services; STO-06 Storage monitoring and lifecycle; CMP-03 Capacity, scheduling and utilisation; RES-04 Recovery planning; RES-05 Testing and exercising
evidence: E4 restore test at the declared concurrent scale (or a validated scaled test with T15 extrapolation) measuring time to all jobs running (V6).
E3 checkpoint write and verification logs showing completion and integrity over a representative period.
E2 scheduler configuration of restart admission limits.
E3 capacity forecasting reports with headroom against retention policy.
scenarios.unknowns: Restore throughput at full scale (U5; US4 on CG-10). Whether the latest checkpoints are complete (U7; US4). Metadata scaling limit (U1; US3).

scenarios.title: BMS remote-vendor credential compromise alters chilled-water setpoints
scenarios.initiatingEvent: An attacker uses a compromised BMS integrator remote-support credential (shared account, persistent VPN, no MFA) to access the BMS supervisory server.
scenarios.preconditions: Vendor remote access is always on. BMS permits setpoint and alarm-limit changes without second approval. Controllers accept setpoints from the supervisory layer without hard limits. Independent temperature monitoring of TCS and facility water does not exist outside the BMS.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → DEGRADED (slow-burn) → EMERGENCY → RECOVERY; analysis shall also consider initiation during MAINTENANCE.

path.text: Compromised vendor credential BYPASSES perimeter controls through the vendor conduit (HUMAN_ACTION by adversary).
Attacker raises chilled-water supply setpoint and widens alarm limits; alarm suppression MASKS the change (M09, M19).
Facility water supply temperature rises gradually; CDU approach temperature consumes margin (DEGRADATION driven by adversary).
TCS supply temperature rises; accelerators throttle (M07 on RF-CMP-01); throughput degrades without obvious alarm.
Attacker optionally disables chiller staging or commands CDU valve closure, which ESCALATES to loss of heat rejection.
Thermal shutdown of accelerators; jobs fail; possible equipment stress.
BMS audit logs altered, causing evidence and attribution loss.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-SEC-01, RF-SEC-02, RF-SEC-05, RF-THM-08, RF-THM-04, RF-THM-03, RF-CMP-01, RF-EVA-01
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Training throughput; availability; isolation and security outcomes; evidence and observability outcomes
safeguards: Cause side: just-in-time vendor access with MFA, approval per session and session recording (interrupts step 1).
Escalation: setpoint hard limits enforced in field controllers, not only in the supervisory layer; two-person approval for setpoint and alarm-limit changes (interrupts step 2).

Detection: independent temperature and flow telemetry from IT-side sensors (accelerator inlet coolant temperature) correlated with BMS values; configuration change detection on BMS (interrupts steps 2–4).
Consequence side: IT power capping on coolant temperature (DELAYS step 6).
Evidence: write-once off-box logging of BMS changes (interrupts step 7).
scenarios.familyText: SUP-06 Remote support and third-party access; SEC-01 Identity and privileged access; SEC-02 Control-plane protection; SEC-03 Network security and segmentation; SEC-05 Detection and response; THM-06 Thermal control, maintenance and recovery; EVA-02 Evidence provenance and quality
evidence: E2 remote-access configuration showing JIT activation, MFA and session recording; E3 sample of session records reconciled to work orders.
E4 test that a setpoint outside hard limits is rejected by the field controller (V5, non-production or authorised window).
E3 correlation between IT-side coolant telemetry and BMS readings over a representative period.
E5 independent OT security assessment against IEC 62443-3-2 zones and conduits.
scenarios.unknowns: Whether vendor accounts are unique and revoked on staff change (U2; US4 on CG-15). Whether controllers enforce limits (U1; US4 on CG-07). Integrity of BMS logs (U7; US2–US3).

scenarios.title: Lithium-ion BESS or UPS battery thermal runaway
scenarios.initiatingEvent: An internal short circuit in a lithium-ion cell of a UPS battery cabinet or BESS module initiates thermal runaway.
scenarios.preconditions: Battery installed in a room adjacent to electrical rooms or data hall. Off-gas detection may not be fitted; battery management system (BMS-battery) alarms are routed to the UPS, not to the fire system. Fire-test evidence for propagation (for example UL 9540A test reports) may not match the installed configuration. Emergency response plan does not address re-ignition.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → EMERGENCY → SHUTDOWN (battery string and possibly UPS) → DEGRADED (UPS without battery) → RECOVERY (long, with replacement).

path.text: Cell runaway releases flammable and toxic off-gas before visible fire (M25 on RF-POW-03).
Off-gas accumulates; without detection and ventilation the room atmosphere can reach deflagration conditions (ESCALATION; CG-04).
Heat PROPAGATES_TO adjacent cells and modules unless module design and spacing CONTAIN it.
Fire detection and suppression act; suppression may not stop cell-level runaway (re-ignition risk); smoke PROPAGATES_VIA shared ventilation to adjacent spaces.

Emergency response requires de-energising the UPS and its battery; the UPS block loses ride-through, so the load is either transferred to bypass (exposed to utility disturbances) or shut down (CONTROL_ACTION or HUMAN_ACTION).
Racks on that block operate without ride-through or are lost; synchronous jobs fail if any participant is affected.
Electrolyte, combustion products and suppressant residue contaminate equipment; environmental release reporting.
Replacement battery modules and cabinet repair have long lead times (DELAYS recovery to NORMAL).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-POW-03, RF-PHY-04, RF-ENV-04, RF-OPS-01, RF-RES-03, RF-SUP-02
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Safety outcomes (primary); availability and capacity of the affected block; recovery outcomes; environmental compliance
safeguards: Cause side: cell and module condition monitoring with thermal and voltage anomaly detection; manufacturer quality and approved sourcing (interrupts step 1).
Escalation: off-gas detection triggering ventilation and alarm; explosion control (venting or exhaust) per the installation's hazard analysis (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: module-level propagation resistance evidenced by large-scale fire testing of the installed configuration; separation distances and fire-rated enclosure (CONTAINS step 3).
Consequence side: fire strategy and emergency response plan specific to lithium-ion, including fire-service liaison, re-ignition watch and safe de-energisation (CONTAINS steps 4–5).
Consequence side: electrical topology where loss of one battery string does not remove ride-through from the whole load (limits step 6).
scenarios.familyText: POW-03 UPS and energy storage; PHY-06 Fire, life safety and emergency interfaces; ENV-05 Hazardous materials and waste; OPS-02 Procedure and work control; RES-06 Crisis and adaptive response; SUP-05 Spares, logistics and obsolescence
evidence: E5 large-scale fire test report for the installed battery product and configuration, reviewed by a competent fire engineer against the installation.
E7 hazard mitigation analysis and explosion-control design calculation for the room.
E4 functional test of off-gas detection and ventilation interlocks (V5).
E1/E4 emergency response plan and exercise record with the fire service (V4).
E3 battery management system telemetry and alarm routing configuration (E2).
scenarios.unknowns: Applicability of fire-test results to the installed configuration (U9; US4 on CG-04). Whether off-gas alarms reach the fire system (U10; US4). Replacement lead time (U2; US3 on CG-10).

scenarios.title: Coolant leak at a rack manifold or quick-disconnect
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A quick-disconnect seal fails or a rack manifold cracks, often during a pressure transient (pump start, valve closure) or after a maintenance reconnection.
scenarios.preconditions: Rack manifold sits above power shelves or busbar connections. Leak detection is a single sensing cable at floor level. The CDU automatically makes up coolant from a reservoir when pressure falls. Per-rack isolation valves are manual.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL or MAINTENANCE → EMERGENCY → DEGRADED (rack isolated) → RECOVERY.

path.text: Pressure transient TRIGGERS seal failure at a degraded quick-disconnect (DEGRADATION, CONTRIBUTES_TO); coolant escapes (M25 on RF-THM-06).
Automatic make-up maintains loop pressure, which MASKS the leak at the CDU and sustains the leak volume.
Coolant reaches power shelves or busbar connections; ESCALATION to electrical fault, arc or tracking (CG-04).
Rack power protection trips; if protection is slow or the fault involves the busway, upstream protection clears a larger section (M05 if miscoordinated).
Rack and possibly row loss; synchronous jobs fail.
Coolant spreads under or between racks to adjacent equipment; floor-level detection alarms only after pooling (DELAYS detection).
Isolation, drying, inspection and requalification of affected equipment before re-energisation (RECOVERY); risk that re-energising wet equipment REINTRODUCES the fault.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-THM-06, RF-THM-02, RF-POW-04, RF-POW-05, RF-CMP-01, RF-OPS-02
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Safety (electrical hazard); availability and capacity of affected racks; physical damage; recovery
safeguards: Cause side: quick-disconnect inspection and replacement interval; pressure-test after any reconnection; soft-start and controlled valve timing to limit transients (interrupts step 1).
Detection: point leak sensors at manifold connections and drip trays; CDU make-up volume and rate alarm and limit (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: physical separation or shielding of fluid connections from energised conductors; automatic per-rack isolation on leak detection (interrupts step 3).
Consequence side: selective protection coordination at rack and busway level (CONTAINS step 4).
Recovery: re-energisation procedure with insulation testing and competent sign-off (interrupts step 7).
scenarios.familyText: THM-03 Liquid cooling systems; THM-05 Fluid quality and leak management; POW-04 Distribution and protection; OPS-02 Procedure and work control; PHY-03 Physical zoning and segregation
evidence: E4 leak-detection functional test with a defined fluid, volume and location at manifold level, recording time to alarm and isolation (V5).
E2 CDU configuration showing make-up limit and alarm settings.
E4 commissioning pressure-test records per rack and after maintenance reconnections.
E7 protection coordination study covering rack power shelves and busway taps.
E1 re-energisation procedure; E6 interview evidence that staff know it.
scenarios.unknowns: Behaviour of make-up logic during leak (U1; US4 on CG-06). Leak detection coverage at manifold height (U5; US4 on CG-04). QD condition across fleet (U5; US3).

scenarios.title: Facility water contamination fouls heat exchangers and cold plates
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A water-treatment failure in an open cooling-tower circuit (dosing pump fault, missed chemistry checks) or construction debris from an expansion tie-in enters the facility water loop.
scenarios.preconditions: Facility water passes through CDU heat exchangers with tight approach-temperature design. Side-stream filtration is undersized or bypassed. Chemistry monitoring is manual and periodic. Flushing and cleanliness requirements for tie-ins are not enforced. TCS fill water and inhibitor are managed by a different team.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → DEGRADED (slow-burn) → EMERGENCY if approach collapses → MAINTENANCE (cleaning) → RECOVERY.

path.text: Chemistry excursion or debris CAUSES fouling and biological growth in the facility loop (DEGRADATION; M07 on RF-THM-07).
Fouling of CDU heat-exchanger plates increases approach temperature (M07 on RF-THM-03) across many CDUs fed by the same loop (COMMON_CAUSE).
TCS supply temperature rises at a given load; accelerators throttle at peak load (M07 on RF-CMP-01).
If TCS is contaminated (HX breach, improper fill or material incompatibility), cold-plate microchannels foul or corrode, which ESCALATES to localised overheating and possible leaks.
Biological growth in cooling towers creates a water-borne pathogen hazard (ESCALATION to CG-04).
Cleaning requires taking CDUs out of service, which reduces resilient capacity (MAINTENANCE state).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-THM-07, RF-THM-03, RF-THM-04, RF-ENV-02, RF-CMP-01, RF-OPS-04
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Training throughput at peak load; resilient cooling capacity; safety; equipment life
safeguards: Cause side: water-treatment programme with continuous chemistry monitoring and alarms; filtration and strainers; flushing and cleanliness acceptance for tie-ins (interrupts step 1).
Detection: approach-temperature trending per CDU heat exchanger with alarm on drift (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: TCS chemistry and material compatibility management with periodic sampling (interrupts step 4).
Escalation: cooling-tower pathogen risk management per applicable regulation (interrupts step 5).
Consequence side: N+1 CDU capacity allowing cleaning without loss of outcome (limits step 6).
scenarios.familyText: THM-05 Fluid quality and leak management; THM-04 Heat rejection and water systems; ENV-03 Water performance; OPS-03 Maintenance and reliability; THM-01 Thermal architecture and capacity
evidence: E3 chemistry monitoring records and laboratory results over a representative period.
E3 approach-temperature trend data per CDU with alarm configuration (E2).
E4 tie-in flushing and cleanliness acceptance records.
E5 independent water-treatment audit.
scenarios.unknowns: TCS chemistry history (U1; US3). Material compatibility of mixed-vendor cold plates and manifolds (U9; US3). Fouling rate (U8; US2).

scenarios.title: Shared fibre route cut defeats diverse connectivity
scenarios.initiatingEvent: Third-party excavation near the site cuts a duct carrying fibre for two carriers that were contracted as diverse.
scenarios.preconditions: Diversity was accepted on carrier assurance without route evidence. Both carriers' circuits enter through different building entries but share a duct or bridge crossing outside the boundary. Inference ingress, inter-site checkpoint replication, remote vendor access and cloud identity services all depend on these circuits. Out-of-band access has no independent path.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → DEGRADED or FAILED (external connectivity) → RECOVERY (carrier repair).

path.text: External excavation TRIGGERS a cut of the shared duct (EXTERNAL_EVENT; COMMON_CAUSE through the shared route).
Both carriers' circuits fail; diversity DEFEATED (M01 on RF-NET-03 frontend and WAN).
Inference ingress lost; inference Service Outcome breached immediately.
Inter-site checkpoint replication stops; recovery-point exposure grows (DELAYS replication).
Cloud-hosted identity or MFA unreachable; operators cannot authenticate to some systems (links to X15).
Remote vendor support unavailable during any concurrent incident (SHARED_RESOURCE).
Remote monitoring of the site lost; site-local evidence must be retained.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-NET-03, RF-NET-04, RF-DEP-02, RF-STO-05, RF-SEC-01, RF-SUP-03
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Inference availability and latency; recovery-point outcome for training; observability
safeguards: Cause side: route-level diversity verified with carrier route evidence to a defined separation, including outside-plant segments (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: third diverse path using different medium (for example a different route or wireless backup) for critical control, OOB and identity traffic (CONTAINS steps 5–6).
Consequence side: inference failover to another site with capacity reserved (limits step 3); local identity fallback (limits step 5).
scenarios.familyText: DEP-02 Shared and common-mode dependencies; DEP-03 External providers and utilities; NET-05 Physical connectivity and optics; NET-04 Management and out-of-band networks; RES-03 Continuity planning
evidence: E5 carrier route documentation with separation evidence, reviewed against physical survey.
E4 failover test of inference ingress to an alternate site (V6).
E4 test that OOB and identity fallback work with all carrier circuits disabled (V5/V6, in an authorised window).
scenarios.unknowns: Carrier route geometry (U2; US4 on CG-03 when diversity is credited). Dependence of identity on WAN (U10; US5 if it affects CG-10 and CG-15).

scenarios.title: Firmware supply-chain defect across the GPU fleet
scenarios.initiatingEvent: An authentic, correctly signed accelerator firmware or driver release contains a defect that, under a specific power or clock state, produces silent data corruption or uncorrectable memory errors.
scenarios.preconditions: Release passes signature validation and functional smoke tests. Rollout policy allows fleet-wide deployment within a short window. Silent data corruption screening is not part of acceptance. Checkpoint retention keeps only a few recent checkpoints. Fleet has no firmware diversity.
scenarios.operatingStates: TRANSITION (rollout) → NORMAL (latent) → DEGRADED (detected) → RECOVERY (rollback and re-training from a known-good checkpoint).

path.text: Defective release is deployed to the fleet; signature validation passes, so authenticity checks do not interrupt it (LATENT, COMMON_CAUSE).
Under the triggering power state, some accelerators compute incorrect results without error indication (M16 / M09 on RF-CMP-01).
Corrupted gradients are incorporated into model state; checkpoints written after onset are corrupted (PROPAGATES_TO RF-STO-04).
Training loss anomalies appear later; detection lag means older good checkpoints may already have been rotated out (DELAYS detection; ESCALATION of progress loss).
Uncorrectable errors on other devices cause node failures and job restarts that CORRELATE_WITH the release.
Recovery requires rollback of firmware across the fleet and re-training from the last verified checkpoint; rollback package availability and compatibility determine duration.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-SUP-01, RF-CMP-04, RF-CMP-01, RF-CMP-05, RF-STO-04, RF-STO-05, RF-RES-04
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Data and model integrity; training completion; compute capacity during rollback
safeguards: Cause side: staged rollout with canary population and soak period including SDC screening tests and burn-in under representative power states (interrupts step 1).
Detection: periodic SDC detection tests and cross-replica result comparison; training-health monitoring (loss and gradient anomalies) with alerts (interrupts steps 2–4).
Consequence side: retention of verified checkpoints spanning more than the expected detection lag; checkpoint integrity validation (limits step 4).
Recovery: tested rollback package and procedure (interrupts step 6).
scenarios.familyText: SUP-04 Software, firmware and update supply; CMP-04 Firmware, driver and compatibility; CMP-05 Compute health and observability; STO-03 Integrity and consistency; STO-05 Checkpoint and recovery services; OPS-05 Change and configuration management
evidence: E1/E4 rollout records showing canary waves, soak duration and SDC test results.
E2 fleet firmware inventory by version and wave.
E4 rollback test on a representative partition (V5).
E3 training-health monitoring alerts and responses.
scenarios.unknowns: OEM defect disclosure (U2/U6; US3). SDC test coverage of triggering conditions (U8; US4 on CG-08). Detection lag (U1; US3).

scenarios.title: Concurrent maintenance exposes a hidden shared electrical dependency
scenarios.initiatingEvent: The A-side UPS and distribution path is taken out of service for planned maintenance.
scenarios.preconditions: Racks are designed dual-corded A/B, but an as-built divergence exists: some rack power shelves have both inputs connected to A-side PDUs, or rack-scale systems with single-input power shelves were added on the A side. The B path's capacity was checked against design load, not measured peak AI load. The method statement does not require verification of cord-to-feed mapping or B-side headroom immediately before isolation.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → MAINTENANCE → FAILED (affected racks) → RECOVERY.

path.text: Planned isolation of the A path (HUMAN_ACTION, ENABLING).
Racks whose both cords are on A lose power (M29 misallocation, LATENT; CAUSES M01 on RF-POW-05 for those racks).
B path carries all remaining load; at peak training load B-side PDUs or busway taps exceed rating and trip (M14), which CASCADES to further rack loss.
Synchronous jobs on affected racks fail; job loss extends to all jobs with any participant on those racks.
Sudden load drop and then restart surge cause cooling-plant control transients (AMPLIFIES).
Maintenance must be aborted and A path restored under time pressure, raising the risk of switching error (links to X16).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-POW-05, RF-POW-04, RF-DEP-01, RF-OPS-02, RF-OPS-03, RF-EVA-02, RF-CMP-01
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Availability and capacity during maintenance (concurrent-maintainability claim); training completion
safeguards: Cause side: periodic as-built audit of cord-to-feed mapping reconciled in EPMS, and per-outlet metering that detects single-path loading (interrupts step 2).

Cause side: pre-isolation readiness check in the method statement: measured B-side load and headroom at expected peak, list of single-path racks, workload drain or power capping applied (interrupts steps 2–3).
Escalation: power capping on B-side overload risk (interrupts step 3).
Consequence side: scheduler drain of single-path racks before maintenance (limits step 4).
scenarios.familyText: OPS-02 Procedure and work control; OPS-05 Change and configuration management; POW-04 Distribution and protection; POW-06 Electrical monitoring, maintenance and recovery; DEP-01 Dependency discovery; EVA-02 Evidence provenance and quality
evidence: E2 EPMS per-outlet load and feed mapping export reconciled to the rack power register (RECONCILIATION).
E1 method statement with readiness checks; E3 record of the checks performed for the last maintenance events.
E4 concurrent-maintenance test with representative load (V6).
scenarios.unknowns: Cord-to-feed mapping for racks added since commissioning (U3; US5 where it bears on both CG-02 and CG-05, otherwise US4 on CG-05). Measured peak B-side load (U1; US4).

scenarios.title: Heatwave combined with water restriction on evaporative heat rejection
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A prolonged heatwave raises ambient wet-bulb temperature above the heat-rejection design condition while the water utility imposes abstraction or supply restrictions.
scenarios.preconditions: Evaporative cooling towers or adiabatic coolers provide most heat rejection. Design ambient was based on historical data without climate projection. On-site water storage autonomy is limited. The grid operator issues demand-response requests in the same period.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → DEGRADED (derated) → EMERGENCY (load shedding) → RECOVERY.

path.text: Ambient exceedance (EXTERNAL_EVENT) CAUSES reduced heat-rejection capacity (M07 on RF-THM-04).
Water restriction CONTRIBUTES_TO further capacity loss as evaporative duty cannot be sustained (AND with step 1; M14 on RF-ENV-02).
Chillers operate at high condensing pressure; some trip on high-pressure protection (M24 if spurious, M01 if genuine), consuming redundancy.
Facility water and TCS supply temperatures rise; accelerators throttle; at the limit, load must be shed.
Grid demand-response obligations and higher cooling power CONFLICT_WITH sustaining full IT load.
Load shedding by priority (graceful degradation) must be executed; if not pre-planned, ad hoc decisions DELAY response.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-THM-04, RF-ENV-02, RF-THM-03, RF-CMP-01, RF-RES-02, RF-CAP-02
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Compute capacity and throughput; availability of lower-priority workloads; environmental compliance (water)
safeguards: Cause side: heat-rejection design and derating at projected extreme ambient; hybrid dry/wet operation (interrupts step 1).
Escalation: water storage autonomy sized for the restriction scenario; alternative supply agreement (interrupts step 2).
Consequence side: pre-approved load-shedding priorities and automated power capping by workload class (limits steps 4–6).
scenarios.familyText: ENV-06 Climate adaptation and resource continuity; ENV-03 Water performance; THM-01 Thermal architecture and capacity; THM-04 Heat rejection and water systems; RES-01 Resilience strategy; CAP-05 Operating envelope
evidence: E7 heat-rejection capacity analysis at projected extreme ambient, with derating curves from equipment data.
E3 performance during the hottest observed periods (V2).
E1 water-supply agreement and storage autonomy calculation.
E4 exercise of load-shedding priorities (V4/V6).
scenarios.unknowns: Extreme-ambient design basis under climate projection (U9; US3–US4). Utility restriction policy (U2; US3).

scenarios.title: Time-source failure causes divergence across control planes
scenarios.initiatingEvent: GNSS signal loss or interference at the grandmaster antennas, or a misconfigured clock wins best-master selection and steps time.
scenarios.preconditions: PTP and NTP hierarchy depends on one GNSS source type; holdover oscillators are limited; clients permit large time steps; the same time hierarchy serves the AI fabric, storage, identity, BMS/EPMS and logging.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → DEGRADED (holdover or wrong time) → RECOVERY.

path.text: GNSS loss TRIGGERS holdover; drift accumulates; or a rogue clock is selected (M09 on RF-NET-05).
Clock offset beyond tolerance causes certificate and token validation failures; operators and services fail to authenticate (PROPAGATES_TO RF-SEC-01).
Distributed storage leases and consensus behave incorrectly; possible metadata inconsistency (M27).
Scheduler timeouts and job failures from skewed heartbeats.
Logs and EPMS sequence-of-events records lose correlation, causing evidence and attribution loss for any concurrent event (MASKS causal reconstruction).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-NET-05, RF-SEC-01, RF-STO-04, RF-CMP-03, RF-POW-07, RF-EVA-01
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Availability; data integrity; observability and evidence
safeguards: Cause side: multiple diverse time sources with authenticated distribution and grandmaster priority settings restricting which clocks can become master (interrupts step 1).
Escalation: holdover oscillator quality sized for the expected outage; client policy to slew rather than step beyond threshold; offset monitoring at every tier with alarms (interrupts steps 2–4).
Evidence: logs carry source and synchronisation status; EPMS has local high-accuracy time-stamping (limits step 5).
scenarios.familyText: NET-06 Network control and observability; SEC-01 Identity and privileged access; STO-03 Integrity and consistency; EVA-02 Evidence provenance and quality
evidence: E2 time-hierarchy configuration including master priorities and client step policy.
E4 GNSS-loss test in holdover with measured drift over the declared holdover period (V5).
E3 offset monitoring history.
scenarios.unknowns: Which systems depend on which time source (U10; US4–US5 depending on gates affected). Holdover performance (U1; US3).

scenarios.title: Recovery reintroduces a corrupt configuration or image
scenarios.initiatingEvent: After an incident caused by a defective configuration change (for example X03) or a defective image, operators restore from the most recent backup.
scenarios.preconditions: Backups are taken on schedule after every change, so the latest backup contains the defect. There is no "known good" tag. The golden image repository has no validation gate. BMS controller backups contain outdated logic or setpoints.
scenarios.operatingStates: FAILED → RECOVERY → FAILED (again) → RECOVERY.

path.text: Recovery selects the latest backup (HUMAN_ACTION under time pressure).
Restore REINTRODUCES the defective configuration or image (RECOVERY_INDUCED).
Original failure recurs; or an older BMS backup removes interlocks added after an earlier incident (M16 on RF-SEC-05 or RF-THM-08).
Repeated failure extends recovery time beyond tolerance and erodes confidence in recovery (DELAYS).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-RES-04, RF-RES-03, RF-OPS-03, RF-CMP-06, RF-NET-02, RF-THM-08
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Recovery time; availability; integrity of configuration
safeguards: Cause side: versioned configuration with known-good tagging and change correlation; restore procedure selects the last validated baseline, not the latest backup (interrupts step 1).
Escalation: validation of restored configuration or image in a staging environment or canary before fleet application (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: BMS and controller backups version-controlled and reconciled to current approved logic (interrupts step 3).
scenarios.familyText: RES-04 Recovery planning; OPS-05 Change and configuration management; CMP-06 Compute lifecycle and recovery; NET-06 Network control and observability; THM-06 Thermal control, maintenance and recovery
evidence: E2 configuration repository showing tagged known-good baselines and correlation to changes.
E4 restore exercise selecting a known-good baseline and validating it (V5/V6).
E1 recovery procedure with validation steps.
scenarios.unknowns: Whether controller backups match the current approved logic (U3; US4 on CG-07). Whether known-good baselines exist for all device classes (U5; US3).

scenarios.title: Shared identity service failure blocks operators and break-glass access during an incident
scenarios.initiatingEvent: The central identity provider or MFA service becomes unavailable (for example through a power event in the hall hosting it, a WAN loss as in X09, or a certificate expiry).
scenarios.preconditions: BMS, EPMS, cluster managers, jump hosts and fabric controllers authenticate against the same identity service. Break-glass accounts are stored in a vault that itself depends on the identity service or is hosted in the same fault domain. Local console access to OT HMIs has been removed.
scenarios.operatingStates: Any → EMERGENCY (if concurrent incident) → RECOVERY.

path.text: Identity service failure (M01 on RF-SEC-01), possibly CASCADING from a power or network event.
Operators cannot log in to BMS, EPMS or cluster managers (SHARED_RESOURCE).
Break-glass procedure depends on the same service or fault domain; break-glass is DEFEATED.
Response to any concurrent incident is DELAYED; automated systems continue unsupervised.
Recovery of the identity service may itself require privileged access that depends on the identity service (circular recovery dependency).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-SEC-01, RF-OPS-01, RF-RES-03, RF-NET-04, RF-GOV-01
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Recovery time of any concurrent incident; availability; control-plane integrity
safeguards: Cause side: identity service deployed across independent fault domains, with local authentication caches at critical systems (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: break-glass credentials held offline in physical custody, independent of the identity service, tested on a schedule (interrupts step 3).
Escalation: local operator panels for safety-relevant OT functions (interrupts step 4).
Recovery: documented, non-circular identity recovery procedure (interrupts step 5).
scenarios.familyText: SEC-01 Identity and privileged access; NET-04 Management and out-of-band networks; RES-04 Recovery planning; DEP-02 Shared and common-mode dependencies; OPS-01 Operating model and staffing
evidence: E4 break-glass test with the identity service disabled (V5, authorised window).
E2 identity-service deployment map against fault domains.
E1 identity recovery procedure; E4 exercise record (V4).
scenarios.unknowns: Dependence of break-glass on identity (U10; US4 on CG-15, US5 if CG-10 also affected). Hosting fault domain of identity components (U10; US4).

scenarios.title: Alarm flood during an electrical event leads to operator mis-switching
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A medium-voltage fault causes loss of one utility feed and multiple automatic transfers, generating thousands of BMS and EPMS alarms within minutes.
scenarios.preconditions: Alarm rationalisation has not been performed; there is no first-out or state-based suppression. Emergency operating procedures are generic. The single-line diagram on the HMI does not match the as-built after recent changes. Staffing at night is minimal.
scenarios.operatingStates: EMERGENCY → FAILED (if mis-switching) → RECOVERY.

path.text: Fault TRIGGERS protection and transfers; alarm flood follows (M20 on RF-OPS-01; DEMAND_SURGE on operators).
Alarm flood MASKS the root alarm; operator misidentifies which side is healthy (HUMAN_ACTION; systemic contributors: interface, alarm load, staffing).
Operator opens the wrong breaker during a manual transfer, dropping the remaining healthy side (M09 on RF-OPS-02).
Load lost across the affected block; cooling pumps and CDUs on that block stop; synchronous jobs fail.
Recovery sequence executed under stress; risk of further error.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-OPS-01, RF-OPS-02, RF-OPS-05, RF-POW-07, RF-EVA-02
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Availability; safety (switching error near energised equipment); recovery time
safeguards: Cause side: alarm rationalisation and state-based suppression with first-out indication (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: event-specific emergency operating procedures with decision aids; two-person verification for switching; key interlocks preventing unsafe breaker combinations (interrupts step 3).
Escalation: HMI single-line diagram reconciled to as-built after every change (interrupts step 2).
Competence: simulator or tabletop training for rare transfer scenarios.
scenarios.familyText: OPS-04 Alarm, incident and problem management; OPS-01 Operating model and staffing; OPS-02 Procedure and work control; POW-06 Electrical monitoring, maintenance and recovery; EVA-02 Evidence provenance and quality
evidence: E3 alarm-rate statistics during past events against the rationalisation target.
E1 emergency operating procedures; E4 exercise records (V4).
E1/E2 interlock schemes and HMI drawing revision control reconciled to as-built.
scenarios.unknowns: HMI as-built accuracy (U3; US3–US4). Night-shift competence for manual transfer (U5; US3).

scenarios.title: Fire in a shared compartment disables paired A/B routes and triggers cascading shutdowns
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A cable fire in a riser or an electrical room in which both A and B feeders (or both fabric trunk routes) pass.
scenarios.preconditions: Route segregation is by tray, not by fire compartment. The fire-alarm cause-and-effect matrix shuts down air handlers and, in one zone, initiates EPO across a wider area than intended. Clean-agent discharge in an adjacent hall requires evacuation and delays re-entry.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → EMERGENCY → FAILED → RECOVERY (extended by damage).

path.text: Cable fault ignites cables (M25); smoke PROPAGATES_VIA the shared compartment.
Both A and B routes are damaged (COMMON_CAUSE through shared compartment; redundancy DEFEATED).
Fire-alarm interface shuts down air handlers in the adjacent hall (CONTROL_ACTION; CONFLICTS_WITH continuity cooling).
EPO initiated over a wider area than the fire zone (M24 spurious extent; M05).
Large-scale loss of compute and storage; unclean shutdown of storage systems.
Re-entry, damage assessment and cable replacement extend recovery; contamination cleaning of equipment.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-PHY-04, RF-POW-05, RF-NET-06, RF-THM-05, RF-RES-01, RF-RES-03
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Safety; availability; capacity; recovery time; physical damage
safeguards: Cause side: segregation of A/B routes into separate fire compartments or fire-rated enclosures (interrupts step 2).
Detection: early-warning smoke detection suited to high-airflow spaces (DELAYS escalation).
Escalation: cause-and-effect matrix verified by integrated test so that shutdown actions are limited to the affected zone (interrupts steps 3–4).
Consequence side: storage systems with protected write caches and orderly-shutdown signals (limits step 5).
scenarios.familyText: PHY-03 Physical zoning and segregation; PHY-06 Fire, life safety and emergency interfaces; POW-04 Distribution and protection; NET-05 Physical connectivity and optics; RES-02 Fault-domain and containment design
evidence: E2/E1 route survey showing compartment of each A/B route, reconciled to drawings.
E4 integrated fire-alarm cause-and-effect test record (V6) witnessed by fire and electrical engineers.
E5 fire-strategy review by a competent fire engineer.
scenarios.unknowns: Whether A/B routes share a compartment at any point (U10; US5 if both CG-05 and CG-09 are affected). Actual extent of EPO zones (U4 if drawings and logic disagree; US4 on CG-04).

scenarios.title: Automated remediation or AI-enabled agent performs a mass action
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A telemetry pipeline defect generates false accelerator error events across a large fraction of nodes; an automated remediation system (or AI-enabled operations agent) drains and reboots the affected nodes, or applies a fleet-wide power cap, in one action.
scenarios.preconditions: Automation has authority to act on any number of nodes; no blast-radius limit or rate limit; no human approval above a threshold; telemetry inputs are not validated for plausibility; power-cap changes have no ramp-rate limit.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → DEGRADED → FAILED (jobs) → RECOVERY.

path.text: Telemetry defect produces false indications (M18 on RF-CMP-05).
Automation acts on the false indications at fleet scale (CONTROL_ACTION; M08 excess output on RF-SEC-03).
Mass drain and reboot terminates many jobs (CASCADE).
Sudden load drop followed by restart surge creates large load steps at UPS and, if on generator, at the generators (DEMAND_SURGE; links to X01).
Cooling-plant control responds to rapid load change; overshoot or undershoot of supply temperature (M13 on RF-THM-08).
Restart storm on provisioning and checkpoint storage (links to X04).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-SEC-03, RF-CMP-05, RF-CMP-06, RF-CAP-01, RF-POW-06, RF-THM-08, RF-STO-03
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Availability; training completion; recovery time; electrical and thermal stability
safeguards: Cause side: plausibility checks on telemetry before automated action (interrupts step 1).
Escalation: blast-radius and rate limits on automated actions; human approval above a node-count or power threshold; command allowlisting (interrupts step 2).
Escalation: ramp-rate limits on fleet power-cap changes (interrupts step 4).
Consequence side: restart admission control (limits step 6).
scenarios.familyText: SEC-06 AI-enabled and automated action; CMP-05 Compute health and observability; CAP-05 Operating envelope; POW-05 Power quality and transient response; THM-06 Thermal control, maintenance and recovery
evidence: E2 automation policy configuration showing limits, approvals and allowlists.
E4 test in a staging environment that an above-threshold action is blocked or held for approval (V5).
E3 automation action logs reconciled to approvals.
scenarios.unknowns: Full set of automation systems with infrastructure authority (U1; US4 on CG-15). Electrical effect of maximum credible load step from automation (U1; US4 on CG-05).

scenarios.title: Colocation density increase silently consumes resilient capacity
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A colocation tenant replaces equipment with a higher-density accelerator generation within its contracted power allocation, but with a less diversified, more synchronous load profile and higher liquid-cooling demand.
scenarios.preconditions: The provider's capacity model assumes diversity across tenants. The tenant's CDUs depend on provider facility water within a supply-temperature band. The shared-responsibility matrix does not specify notification of load-profile change or of provider plant maintenance. The tenant has no evidence rights to provider plant telemetry.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL (apparent) → MAINTENANCE (provider chiller maintenance) → DEGRADED → EMERGENCY.

path.text: Tenant load-profile change (DEMAND_SURGE in peak terms) CONTRIBUTES_TO loss of provider headroom (M14 on RF-CAP-02), LATENT because contracted kW are not exceeded.
Responsibility gap: neither party analyses the combined effect (M17 on RF-DEP-02).
Provider takes one chiller out for maintenance assuming N+1 exists (ENABLING; HUMAN_ACTION).
At peak load, facility water supply temperature exceeds the tenant CDU's band (M07 on RF-THM-04).
Tenant accelerators throttle; jobs slow or fail.
Contractual dispute over responsibility; evidence missing on both sides, producing evidence and attribution loss.

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-CAP-02, RF-DEP-02, RF-THM-04, RF-THM-03, RF-GOV-02, RF-EVA-01
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Tenant training throughput; provider service levels; contractual commitments
safeguards: Cause side: shared-responsibility record that requires notification and joint assessment of load-profile changes; provider capacity model using measured peak and correlation (interrupts steps 1–2).
Escalation: provider maintenance readiness check against measured load; notification to tenants (interrupts step 3).
Detection: tenant monitoring of facility water supply temperature at CDU inlet with alerts; shared telemetry (interrupts step 4).
scenarios.familyText: DEP-05 Boundary and interface control; SUP-02 Contract and service obligations; CAP-04 Demand and growth modelling; THM-01 Thermal architecture and capacity; OPS-06 Capacity and service operations
evidence: E1 shared-responsibility record and contract clauses for notification and evidence rights.
E3 measured peak load and supply-temperature data at CDU inlets.
E7 provider resilient-capacity calculation with measured tenant profiles.
scenarios.unknowns: Provider resilient capacity (U2; US4 on CG-06). Other tenants' load profiles (U2; US3).

scenarios.title: Compound regional event: flood, extended grid loss, telecom loss and fuel logistics
scenarios.initiatingEvent: A regional storm causes river flooding, extended grid outage, loss of public telecom and road closures around the site.
scenarios.preconditions: Ground-level switchgear and fuel tank fill points lie within a credible flood extent; fuel autonomy is sized for a delivery interval that assumes open roads; fuel suppliers are regional and share the same roads; staff relief depends on public transport; generators have not run for an extended duration recently; fuel quality has not been tested for some time.
scenarios.operatingStates: NORMAL → EMERGENCY → DEGRADED (on generators, extended) → possible SHUTDOWN (controlled) → RECOVERY.

path.text: Flood threatens switchgear and fuel-system equipment (EXTERNAL_EVENT).
Grid loss (EXTERNAL_EVENT, CORRELATES_WITH step 1) TRIGGERS generator operation for an extended period.
Extended running reveals fuel contamination or filter blockage (LATENT; M21 on RF-POW-02); one or more generators fail; K_OF_N redundancy at risk.
Road closures and regional demand prevent fuel replenishment (M10 on RF-SUP-02 and RF-DEP-02; DELAYS replenishment beyond autonomy).
Public telecom loss removes WAN and remote support (links to X09, X15).
Staff fatigue and inability to relieve shifts (HUMAN_ACTION contributors).

Decision to degrade to minimum Service Outcome, migrate workloads or execute a controlled shutdown before fuel exhaustion; if not pre-decided, decision delay increases the probability of uncontrolled shutdown (M23).

scenarios.requiredFunctions: RF-PHY-05, RF-POW-02, RF-SUP-02, RF-DEP-02, RF-NET-03, RF-OPS-05, RF-RES-02, RF-RES-05, RF-GOV-01
scenarios.serviceOutcomes: Availability; recovery; safety (flood and fuel handling); strategic or sovereignty outcomes if workloads must move
safeguards: Cause side: flood protection of critical plant above the credible flood level; site hazard assessment (interrupts step 1).
Escalation: fuel quality testing and polishing programme; periodic extended-duration generator runs (interrupts step 3).
Escalation: fuel autonomy sized for the replenishment scenario, multiple suppliers with priority contracts and independent routes (interrupts step 4).
Consequence side: pre-approved crisis priorities, graceful degradation and controlled shutdown plan; staff welfare and accommodation plan (limits steps 6–7).
Consequence side: alternate site capacity with tested migration (limits step 7).
scenarios.familyText: PHY-01 Site and location resilience; POW-02 Generation and fuel; SUP-05 Spares, logistics and obsolescence; RES-03 Continuity planning; RES-06 Crisis and adaptive response; ENV-06 Climate adaptation and resource continuity; OPS-01 Operating model and staffing
evidence: E7 site flood assessment and plant elevation survey.
E4 extended-duration generator run records and fuel quality test results.
E1 fuel supply contracts, autonomy calculation and replenishment plan; E4 crisis exercise (V4).
E4 workload migration test to alternate capacity (V6).
scenarios.unknowns:
Fuel supplier performance under regional event (U2; US4 on CG-05). Credible flood extent under updated projections (U9; US3–US4). Staff availability (U5; US3).

## Scenario prioritisation

Scenarios shall be prioritised for analysis depth and validation effort when any of the following apply; each criterion is linked to the gate it most directly engages.

| **Priority criterion** | **Primary gate** |
|------------------------|------------------|
| Life safety or hazardous energy | CG-04 |
| Essential cooling loss | CG-06 |
| Standby or resilient power loss | CG-05 |
| Containment failure | CG-09 |
| Large capability concentration | CG-03 |
| Checkpoint or recovery-baseline corruption | CG-10 |
| Common-mode defeat of redundancy | CG-09 |
| Recovery objective at risk | CG-10 |
| Weakly evidenced external dependency | CG-03 |
| Long-lead or irreplaceable component | CG-10 |
| Control-plane or remote-access exposure | CG-15 |
| Sovereignty impact | CG-01 |
| Critical UNKNOWN (US4 or US5) | CG-12 |
